Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• Sudden onset severe unilateral (left) headache awakening patient at 05:30, photophobia, minimal relief with paracetamol, no fever, meningism, or focal neurology.  
• History of episodic less-severe headaches; current stress and sleep deprivation.  
• Background generalized anxiety disorder.

Working diagnosis  
Migraine without aura (high likelihood per DDx and clinical features) vs tension-type headache.

Differential considerations (consistent with DDx)  
• Tension-type headache – medium likelihood; stress-related, prior similar but milder; less compatible with unilateral pain and photophobia.  
• Cluster headache – low-medium likelihood; early-morning unilateral pain but lacks autonomic signs.  
• Subarachnoid hemorrhage – low likelihood but serious; currently no red-flag features beyond abrupt onset.  

Management / plan  
• Start Ibuprofen (higher migraine dose) ± continue paracetamol as needed.  
• Advise hydration 1.5–2 L water/day (excluding caffeinated drinks).  
• Encourage 7–8 hrs nightly sleep; consider 1-week sick leave to reduce work stress.  
• Provide self-referral link to local counseling service for stress management.  
• Supply patient information on headache red-flag symptoms; instruct to seek urgent review if red flags develop.  
• Schedule follow-up in 1 week; consider blood tests or imaging if no improvement or new concerning features.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Discussed sleep hygiene, hydration, stress reduction, and appropriate analgesic use.  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Relief of current headache; reduce work-related stress; maintain regular exercise.

- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  Follow-up telehealth review in 1 week arranged; advised earlier review if symptoms worsen.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Migraine without aura – High likelihood: unilateral severe pain, photophobia, stress/sleep deprivation trigger.  
2. Tension-type headache – Medium likelihood: ongoing work stress, anxiety history; less typical due to unilateral pain.  
3. Cluster headache – Low-Medium likelihood: early-morning unilateral pain but lacks autonomic features.
